newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares drift, watch for Mosenergo news.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares drift, watch for Mosenergo news.

text.p: Russian shares drifted about a percentage point down at the opening on Monday and traders said only the annual meeting of regional power utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS could weakly move the market.
Traders expected a thin, range-bound market through the day and the week, with no major Russian events in sight and Wall Street consolidating.

Trinfiko senior trader Grigory Pensky said Mosenergo shareholders' approval of dividends and investment plans could spur some support, but no more than a two percent gain since divisive issues were dropped from the agenda last week.
Mosenergo shareholders meet on Monday but proposals to limit voting rights and authorise a share issue were dropped from the agenda last week.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index opened almost unchanged at 299.30 after 299.06 at the close on Friday and early volume was average.

At 0845 GMT, oil producer LUKoil prefs LKOH_p.RTS rose to $10.30 from $10.15, national electricity company UES EESR.RTS had slipped to $0.2180 from $0.2215 and Mosenergo had ticked down to $1.278 from $1.293.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's Pavel Gronbjerg said Western eyes were still glued to Wall Street. The Dow has regained about half of its 10 percent losses in mid-March to mid-April but is still seen finding its feet.
"Hedge funds don't like to see the whole world crashing and then go in and buy Russia," Gronbjerg said.
Traders said Russian investors, including banks, had bought some leading shares which Westerners had been unaggressively selling.

"The first five bids on LUKoil are all in roubles," said Rinaco Plus trader Tom Brackenbury. Foreign investors generally put bids in dollars. "That suggests the interest is mainly local." But local interest is also weak, he said.
